meta.name: cw4_gold
meta.eval_gate: asymmetric cost-matrix gold set; quote survival
how_the_labels_were_arrived_at: The ladder is the POC's own: EVIDENCE_ORDER in app/candidate_profile.py. No parallel scale was invented.
Each row asks one question: what does THIS quote, from THIS project, prove about THIS skill?
none = the quote proves nothing about the skill. It may be a real quote, from the right project, and still be about something else. This is a correct answer, not a refusal.
mentioned = the skill is named or plainly present, but no work with it by the candidate is separable from the quote (a stack line, someone else's work, team work, a tool being removed).
demonstrated = the candidate personally did something with the skill.
led = the candidate personally owned it, or made a named decision inside it. Team language never supports led (RULEBOOK 13, weaker-wins); passive attribution ('led by my manager') never supports led.
Grounding is out of scope here: every quote is treated as verbatim candidate text, because substring grounding is already solved in code. CW-4 judges aboutness and strength, not existence.
Where the POC's house rule and a loose human reading disagree, the house rule wins and the row is tagged 'borderline' with the disagreement named in `why`.

slices.d10: The defect class the workload exists to catch: a real quote about something ADJACENT to the skill (Terraform rated 'demonstrated' on 'I ran the schema migrations'). These rows matter most.
slices.team: Team-vs-self. 'we migrated...', 'the team chose...' - real work, but the candidate's own part is not separable.
slices.passive: Passive / attribution traps: 'led by my manager', 'I was asked to', 'under the direction of'.
slices.stack_list: The skill appears only in a comma-separated stack line - 'mentioned' at best.
slices.borderline: A reasonable rater could argue one rung either way. A disagreement here should be read differently from a disagreement on a clear case.

meta.caveat: SYNTHETIC AND UNREVIEWED. Every person, company and project below is invented (HUM-3: no real resumes, no real people). The labels are one author's judgement, written in one sitting, with no second rater and no inter-rater agreement measured. The reference says the real CW-4 gold set needs human raters; this is a stand-in that lets the scorer be built and tested offline. It is not a Caliber number.
meta.counts_are_not_stored: Level distribution and slice sizes are computed by evals/cw4.py from the rows, never written here, so they cannot drift.

claims.project: RAG assistant over clinical policy documents (Northwind Health)
claims.quote: I chose hybrid search over pure vector search in pgvector after recall on drug names was poor, and owned the retrieval redesign
claims.why: First person, a named decision taken inside pgvector itself, and stated ownership of the redesign. The clearest 'led' shape there is.

claims.quote: I designed the Kafka partitioning scheme and decided on keyed compaction for the shipment topic
claims.why: Two ownership verbs (designed, decided) applied to Kafka internals, not to the project around it.

claims.quote: I owned the Airflow scheduler migration and chose to move the DAGs to deferrable operators
claims.why: Ownership plus a named technical choice within Airflow.

claims.quote: I architected the Terraform module layout and decided every environment would share one state backend
claims.why: A design decision about Terraform's own structure, made by the candidate.

claims.project: Newsroom research assistant, RAG over the archive (Sparrowhawk Media)
claims.quote: I designed the prompt evaluation harness and chose pairwise grading over a single absolute score
claims.why: A method decision with the alternative named - the strongest evidence shape the ladder has.

claims.quote: I owned the Postgres schema for the ledger and decided to keep balances as an append-only table
claims.why: Ownership of the Postgres artefact plus a modelling decision inside it.

claims.project: RAG assistant over clinical policy documents (Northwind Health)
claims.quote: Cut average answer latency from 9s to 3s by caching embeddings (Redis)
claims.why: The candidate did the caching and Redis is the instrument of it. No decision is named, so not led.

claims.quote: Trained and deployed churn prediction models for a telecom client (Python, scikit-learn, Airflow)
claims.why: 'Trained and deployed' is work the candidate did, and scikit-learn is the tool training runs in. Compare cw4-016: the same sentence proves far less about Airflow.

claims.quote: I wrote the FastAPI endpoints that serve the turbine telemetry to the control room
claims.why: First-person authorship of FastAPI code; nothing about owning or deciding.

claims.quote: I cleaned eleven years of manifest data in pandas before any model saw it
claims.why: Work the candidate did, in the named tool.

claims.quote: I containerised the settlement worker with Docker and ran it locally against the sandbox
claims.why: Hands on Docker, no ownership claim.

claims.quote: I wrote and tested the dbt models for the finance mart
claims.why: Authorship of dbt models. 'Wrote and tested' is work, not a decision.

claims.project: RAG assistant over clinical policy documents (Northwind Health)
claims.quote: Built a RAG assistant that answers clinicians' policy questions over 40k internal documents (LangChain, pgvector, OpenAI)
claims.why: 'Built' plus the tool in the parenthetical stack of the thing built. Weaker than cw4-001 on the same project because no decision is named.

claims.quote: I built the Grafana dashboard the on-call engineer opens first
claims.why: Built it personally; the sentence claims usefulness, not ownership of the practice.

claims.quote: I backfilled pytest coverage for the claims engine from 14% to 71%
claims.why: Measurable personal work in the named tool.

claims.quote: (Python, scikit-learn, Airflow)
claims.why: A bare stack parenthetical. The tool was present on the project; the quote shows nobody doing anything with it.

claims.quote: Stack: Go, Kubernetes, Postgres, Terraform, Datadog
claims.why: Tool-in-a-list. 'mentioned' is the ceiling for a stack line, whatever the model's enthusiasm.

claims.quote: Stack: Go, Kubernetes, Postgres, Terraform, Datadog
claims.why: Same line, same ceiling. Two rows from one stack line, so a scorer can see the level is a property of the sentence and not of the tool.

claims.quote: We added an LLM-as-judge evaluation step before releases (Ragas, various tools)
claims.why: Both traps at once: team language AND a stack parenthetical. Either alone caps at mentioned.

claims.quote: The platform team exposes a GraphQL gateway that our service registers with
claims.why: GraphQL really is in the candidate's working world and the sentence is real - but every verb belongs to the platform team or to the service, never to the candidate.

claims.quote: Familiar with Spark, Flink and Beam
claims.why: A self-assessment in a list. 'Familiar with' is the candidate rating themselves, which is exactly what the evidence ladder exists to replace.

claims.quote: We are partway through an OpenTelemetry rollout
claims.why: Team subject, unfinished work, no personal act. The skill is present; nothing is proven.

claims.project: RAG assistant over clinical policy documents (Northwind Health)
claims.quote: Cut average answer latency from 9s to 3s by caching embeddings (Redis)
claims.why: A real quote, from a real project of theirs, that says nothing at all about Kubernetes. The baseline shape the D10 rows complicate.

claims.project: Newsroom research assistant, RAG over the archive (Sparrowhawk Media)
claims.quote: I designed the prompt evaluation harness and chose pairwise grading over a single absolute score
claims.why: A strong 'led' quote - for a different skill. Strength of language must not leak across skills.

claims.quote: I owned the Postgres schema for the ledger
claims.why: Technical ownership says nothing about a non-technical skill.

claims.quote: I containerised the settlement worker with Docker and ran it locally against the sandbox
claims.why: Terraform is simply absent. Compare cw4-031, which is the same quote against a far more tempting skill.

claims.quote: I wrote the FastAPI endpoints that serve the turbine telemetry to the control room
claims.why: Serving data implies a store somewhere, but implication is not evidence.

claims.quote: I backfilled pytest coverage for the claims engine from 14% to 71%
claims.why: Solo technical work is not evidence of a people skill.

claims.quote: I ran the schema migrations by hand before each release
claims.why: The canonical D10 shape, taken from the reference. Real quote, right project, first person, release-infrastructure flavoured - and it proves nothing about Terraform. 'By hand' is in fact the opposite of infrastructure-as-code.

claims.quote: I wrote the Airflow DAG that loads the nightly snapshot into the warehouse
claims.why: Adjacent by category - both move data - and a genuinely strong quote for Airflow. Nothing here streams; nothing here is Kafka.

claims.quote: I containerised the settlement worker with Docker and ran it locally against the sandbox
claims.why: The tempting adjacency: containers are what Kubernetes schedules. But building an image and running it locally is exactly the part of the story where Kubernetes is not involved.

claims.project: Newsroom research assistant, RAG over the archive (Sparrowhawk Media)
claims.quote: I tuned the BM25 field weights until the newsroom stopped complaining about recall
claims.why: Same problem (recall), same project, opposite technology: BM25 is lexical, pgvector is vector. Strong evidence for retrieval, zero for pgvector.

claims.project: RAG assistant over clinical policy documents (Northwind Health)
claims.quote: I chose hybrid search over pure vector search in pgvector after recall on drug names was poor
claims.why: The same sentence that earns 'led' in cw4-001. A decision verb plus an LLM-shaped project invites a verdict for anything LLM-adjacent; the decision is about retrieval, not prompts.

claims.quote: I wrote the JSON schema the front end validates against
claims.why: Front-end adjacency plus the word 'schema'. No language is named, and JSON is not TypeScript.

claims.quote: I replayed last quarter's traffic offline against the new pricing model
claims.why: BORDERLINE. An offline replay is counterfactual evaluation, not a controlled online experiment - no arms, no randomisation, no live users. A rater reading 'A/B testing' loosely as 'experimentation' would say mentioned. I hold none; a disagreement here is a definition dispute, not a model failure.

claims.quote: I added a retry with exponential backoff around the flaky vendor call
claims.why: Reliability work sits next to observability in every job advert and is not it. Nothing is measured, emitted or alerted on.

claims.quote: The manifests arrive in the Snowflake warehouse the analytics team owns
claims.why: BORDERLINE. The skill is named in the candidate's own text and is genuinely part of their working environment, which is more than cw4-029 has - so mentioned, not none. But the only actor is the analytics team. A rater who requires the candidate's own contact for 'mentioned' would say none.

claims.quote: We replaced Jenkins with GitHub Actions in my first month
claims.why: BORDERLINE. Jenkins is named, and named as the thing being removed - the skill actually demonstrated is GitHub Actions. Removing something does require knowing it, so mentioned rather than none; 'we' caps it there anyway. A rater could argue none, on the grounds that the quote is evidence against current Jenkins practice.

claims.quote: I ran the audit job on the Databricks workspace the platform team set up
claims.why: BORDERLINE. Databricks runs Spark, so a model that knows the ecosystem will reach for demonstrated. The quote never says the candidate wrote, tuned or even saw Spark - they ran a job on a platform someone else built. Mentioned is the honest ceiling.

claims.project: RAG assistant over clinical policy documents (Northwind Health)
claims.quote: I chose hybrid search over pure vector search in pgvector after recall on drug names was poor
claims.why: BORDERLINE, and the most interesting row in the set. pgvector IS a Postgres extension, so unlike cw4-033 this quote really is about Postgres work - demonstrated is right. But the decision named is a retrieval decision, not a Postgres one, so the 'led' the same sentence earns for pgvector must not transfer. The error to catch here is 'led', not 'demonstrated'.

claims.quote: I wrote and tested the dbt models for the finance mart
claims.why: BORDERLINE. A dbt model is a SELECT statement, so writing one is writing SQL - but the word never appears and the inference is domain knowledge, not reading. Demonstrated because the containment is total rather than merely adjacent; a strict rater would say mentioned.

claims.quote: I reviewed the Terraform plan output before my colleague applied it
claims.why: BORDERLINE. Real, first-person, named contact with Terraform - but reviewing a plan is the weakest form of it, and the applying was someone else's. Demonstrated; a strict rater could say mentioned. Pairs with cw4-004 to show the same skill and candidate two rungs apart.

claims.quote: I built the Grafana dashboard the on-call engineer opens first
claims.why: Dashboards plus monitoring vocabulary, and no model anywhere in the project. The word 'monitoring' in the skill name is doing all of the tempting.

claims.project: Newsroom research assistant, RAG over the archive (Sparrowhawk Media)
claims.quote: I tuned the BM25 field weights until the newsroom stopped complaining about recall
claims.why: BORDERLINE. Retrieval tuning inside a retrieval-augmented assistant is RAG work, so unlike cw4-032 the adjacency here is containment: demonstrated. But nothing in the quote touches generation, grounding or citation, so a rater who reads RAG as the whole pipeline would say mentioned.

claims.quote: I owned the Postgres schema for the ledger and decided to keep balances as an append-only table
claims.why: A very strong quote, about a database, for a database skill it has nothing to do with. Category adjacency at its most misleading - and note that Postgres CAN be a vector database (cw4-040), just not here.

claims.quote: We migrated the routing service to Kubernetes over two quarters
claims.why: Real Kubernetes work happened and the candidate was in the room. The quote does not separate their part from the team's, and RULEBOOK 13 puts team language at mentioned. The right response is to probe, not to credit.

claims.quote: The team chose GraphQL over REST for the new content API
claims.why: A decision with the alternative named - the exact shape of a 'led' quote - except the subject is the team. Decision language must not survive a change of subject.

claims.quote: Our team rewrote the Airflow DAGs to be idempotent
claims.why: BORDERLINE. 'Our team rewrote' almost certainly includes the candidate writing some DAGs, so demonstrated is arguable. The house rule is that team language is not personal evidence, and idempotency is precisely the kind of design credit that should be probed rather than assumed.

claims.quote: Maintained the team's model monitoring dashboards (Grafana)
claims.why: 'The team's' is possessive team language: the artefact belongs to the team. Maintaining is real work, which is why this one is tempting, but the ownership marker sits on the wrong noun.

claims.quote: Together with the platform team I split the Terraform state per environment
claims.why: BORDERLINE. 'I split' is a first-person act on Terraform's own structure, which reads as demonstrated or even led. 'Together with' is a team phrase in app/policy.py and caps it at mentioned. This row exists to measure exactly that disagreement between a plain reading and the house rule.

claims.quote: We ran a blameless postmortem after every Sev-1
claims.why: A practice the candidate was inside, described with a team subject and no personal act.

claims.quote: The Kafka partitioning design was led by my manager
claims.why: The trap: 'led' is in the sentence and the skill is in the sentence, and neither belongs to the candidate. Passive attribution to someone else. Compare cw4-002 - the same skill and the same design, actively owned.

claims.quote: I was asked to apply the Terraform changes the platform team had written
claims.why: BORDERLINE, and the row that keeps the passive rule honest. 'I was asked to' removes 'led'; it does not remove the fact that the candidate personally ran the apply. Over-demoting this to mentioned is an error too - a cheap one, but this set should be able to see it.

claims.quote: Under the direction of the principal engineer I implemented the account hierarchy
claims.why: They did the modelling work; someone else directed it. Demonstrated, never led.

claims.project: Newsroom research assistant, RAG over the archive (Sparrowhawk Media)
claims.quote: The evaluation harness was designed by a contractor before I joined
claims.why: Passive, plus an explicit statement that the candidate was not there. Contrast cw4-005, where the same candidate designed a harness on a different project - the project context, not the vocabulary, is what separates them.

claims.quote: I was asked to document the Airflow DAGs, not to change them
claims.why: First person and a real task, but the sentence itself fences off the engineering work. Reading the DAGs is contact, not practice.
